Bash(/tmp/executive_summary.md << 'EOF' # Word-by-Word Style Override System - Executive Summary ## What is Already Built The Clippify editor has a **fully functional word-by-word style override system** that allows users to customize individual word styling within captions while in word-by-word or other display modes. --- ## Current Capabilities Users can override these properties **per-word**: - **Text Color** \(`color`\) - Change word text color - **Font Weight** \(`fontWeight`\) - Make words bold \(900\) or normal - **Scale** \(`scale`\) - Enlarge words \(1.2x = 20% larger\) - **Emphasis Background** \(`emphasisBg`\) - Add background highlight color --- ## User Workflow ### 1. Select a Word In the **Transcript Panel**, user clicks on any word: ``` [I] [want] [to] [learn] [TypeScript] ↑ Click here ``` ### 2. WordToolbar Appears A toolbar appears with styling controls: ``` [B] [↔] [🎨] [🖍] [✕] Bold Scale Color Highlight Clear ``` ### 3. Apply Styles User clicks buttons or picks colors to apply overrides to that word. ### 4. Visual Feedback - Words with overrides show a **dotted underline** in the transcript - During playback, the word displays with the custom style - Clicking the word again highlights it with the selection ring ### 5. See Changes in Real-Time The preview video updates immediately to show the styled word. --- ## Technical Architecture ### Data Model ``` CaptionItemData { text: string words: [ CaptionWord { text: "hello" startMs: 0 endMs: 500 styleOverrides?: { color?: "#ff0000" fontWeight?: 900 scale?: 1.2 emphasisBg?: "#ffff00" } }, CaptionWord { text: "world" ... } ] style: CaptionStyle // Base caption style } ``` ### State Management \(Zustand Store\) ``` EditorStore { items: { "caption-1": TimelineItem { data: CaptionItemData { ... } } } actions: { updateWordStyleOverrides\(captionId, wordIndex, overrides\) } } ``` ### Rendering Pipeline ``` Remotion Player ↓ passes CaptionItemData AnimatedSubtitle Component ↓ maps over words array Word Component \(per word\) ↓ reads word.styleOverrides ↓ merges with caption style Final CSS applied ↓ Styled word rendered ``` --- ## Key Files and Responsibilities | Component | File | Responsibility | |-----------|------|-----------------| | **Types** | `store/types.ts` | Define WordStyleOverrides, CaptionWord | | **Store** | `store/editor-store.ts` | updateWordStyleOverrides action \(store state mutation\) | | **Hooks** | `store/use-editor-store.ts` | useEditorActions hook \(expose action to UI\) | | **Selection** | `panels/TranscriptPanel.tsx` | Word selection UI, visual indicators | | **Controls** | `panels/WordToolbar.tsx` | Color/bold/scale/highlight controls | | **Rendering** | `renderer/AnimatedSubtitle.tsx` | Apply overrides to CSS | --- ## How Word Overrides Are Applied When rendering a word, the system applies overrides with this priority: ``` IF word.styleOverrides exists THEN fontSize = word.styleOverrides.scale * baseStyle.fontSize fontWeight = word.styleOverrides.fontWeight OR baseStyle.fontWeight color = word.styleOverrides.color OR baseStyle.color \(or activeColor if active\) backgroundColor = word.styleOverrides.emphasisBg OR baseStyle.backgroundColor ELSE Use all base style properties ``` **Example:** ``` Base style: fontSize=48px, color=white, fontWeight=400 Word overrides: { color: "red", scale: 1.2 } Result: fontSize=57.6px, color=red, fontWeight=400 ``` --- ## Store Action - updateWordStyleOverrides **Signature:** ```typescript updateWordStyleOverrides\( captionId: string, // Which caption wordIndex: number, // Which word \(0-based\) overrides: Partial | null // What to apply \) => void ``` **Behaviors:** 1. **Apply overrides:** `updateWordStyleOverrides\(id, 0, { color: "#ff0000" }\)` - Merges with existing overrides - Cleans out undefined values 2. **Partial update:** `updateWordStyleOverrides\(id, 0, { fontWeight: 900 }\)` - Keeps existing color, scale, emphasisBg - Only updates fontWeight 3. **Clear all:** `updateWordStyleOverrides\(id, 0, null\)` - Removes all overrides from word - Reverts to base caption style **Important:** Does NOT auto-save \(unlike caption-level style updates\). Changes are saved when user saves project. --- ## Visual Indicators in UI ### Transcript Panel Word Rendering ```typescript {/* Normal word */} hello {/* Active word \(during playback\) */} hello {/* Word with overrides */} hello {/* Selected word */} hello ``` ### WordToolbar Visual States ``` [B] - Bold button [ ] Normal - clicked shows "fontWeight: 900" state [⬚] Active - highlighted in accent color when bold is applied [↔] - Scale button [ ] 1.0x - normal state [⬚] 1.2x - active state when scaled [🎨] [🖍] - Color pickers Show current selected color [✕] - Clear all Resets word to base style ``` --- ## Integration Points ### For WordToolbar to Control Words ```typescript import { useEditorActions } from '../store/use-editor-store'; function WordToolbar\(\) { const { updateWordStyleOverrides } = useEditorActions\(\); // User clicks color picker updateWordStyleOverrides\(captionId, wordIndex, { color: newColor }\); } ``` ### For Custom Components to Access Words ```typescript import { useSingleSelectedItem } from '../store/use-editor-store'; function MyComponent\(\) { const item = useSingleSelectedItem\(\); // Gets selected caption const words = \(item?.data as CaptionItemData\)?.words; words.forEach\(\(word, index\) => { if \(word.styleOverrides?.color\) { // Word has color override } }\); } ``` ### For Renderer to Apply Styles ```typescript // In AnimatedSubtitle.tsx - Word component const overrides = word.styleOverrides; const wordCss = { fontSize: \(overrides?.scale || 1\) * baseFontSize, fontWeight: overrides?.fontWeight || baseFontWeight, color: overrides?.color || baseColor, backgroundColor: overrides?.emphasisBg || baseBg, }; ``` --- ## What's NOT Overridable Per-Word \(and Why\) Cannot override per-word \(caption-level only\): - ❌ **fontFamily** - Would need complex font loading per-word - ❌ **lineHeight** - Affects whole caption layout - ❌ **position** - Position is for entire caption box - ❌ **animation** - Animation timing tied to caption duration - ❌ **displayMode** - Mode applies to all words in caption - ❌ **effects** \(shadows, glow\) - Complex rendering, expensive - ❌ **stroke** \(outline\) - Would require per-word text rendering - ❌ **textTransform** - Better handled at display level --- ## Edge Cases & Behaviors ### What happens when caption style changes? - Overrides are preserved - Base style updates, overrides still apply on top - Example: If fontWeight changes from 400→700, word with `fontWeight: 900` still shows 900 ### What happens when caption is split? - Overrides are preserved on original words - New words created from split have no overrides ### What happens when captions are merged? - Both sets of word overrides are preserved - Words keep their styling from original captions ### What about undo/redo? - Each `updateWordStyleOverrides` call pushes history - User can undo word styling changes - Separate from caption-level style undo/redo --- ## Missing Features \(Not Implemented\) Could be added in future: - Font size override per-word \(currently only scale\) - Letter spacing per-word - Text shadow/glow per-word - Animation variation per-word - Batch apply overrides to multiple words - Copy overrides from one word to another - Preset word styles \(e.g., "emphasis", "highlight"\) --- ## Performance Considerations ### Current State - Efficient: Only mutates the specific word - Immer middleware handles immutability automatically - Re-renders only affected UI components - Renderer only processes overrides if present ### No Performance Issues - Word selection doesn't loop through all words - Override application is O\(1\) per word - No watchers or deep comparisons needed --- ## Testing Checklist To verify the system works end-to-end: 1. Load project with captions 2. Click a word in Transcript Panel → Toolbar appears 3. Toggle bold → Word shows bold in preview 4. Pick color → Word shows new color in preview 5. Toggle scale → Word appears larger 6. Pick highlight color → Word shows background 7. Clear all → Word reverts to base style 8. Reload page → Overrides are preserved \(if saved\) 9. Undo → Previous state restored 10. Preview video → Styled words render correctly --- ## Summary The word-by-word override system is **production-ready** with: - Clean type definitions - Efficient store mutations - Good UX with visual feedback - Proper undo/redo support - No performance issues - Safe renderer integration The system is extensible and could support additional per-word properties if needed in the future. EOF)
